messages.subject: Challenging stochastic vol model
parts:
Hi all,

I'm working with version of the Kim et al. stochastic volatility model of discussed at p75-8 of the 2.6.2 manual. I want to drop the assumption of independence between the volatility shocks \delta_t and the shocks \epsilon_t related to observations. However, I'm having a hard time expressing the result in a way that preserves vectorization, standardized parameters, etc. My best attempt so far (below) is slow, so I would appreciate any tips. 

A csv of some data for 'y' is attached.

Thanks,
John



data {
    int<lower = 1> T;
    vector[T] y;
}
parameters {
    real mu;
    real<lower=-1,upper=1> phi;
    vector[T] log_sigma2;
    real<lower=0> sigma_delta;
    corr_matrix[2] Omega;
}
transformed parameters{
    vector[2] y_delta[T];

    for(t in 1:T)
        y_delta[t,1] <- y[t];
    
    y_delta[1,2] <- log_sigma2[1] - mu;
    for(t in 2:T)
        y_delta[t,2] <- log_sigma2[t] - mu - phi*(log_sigma2[t-1]-mu);    
}
model{
    matrix[2,2] Sigma;
    vector[2] tau;
    tau[2] <- sigma_delta;
    
    mu ~ cauchy(0,5);
    phi ~ uniform(-1,1);
    sigma_eta ~ cauchy(0,5);
    Omega ~ lkj_corr(2);

    for(t in 1:T){
        tau[1] <- exp(log_sigma2[t]/2);
        Sigma <- quad_form_diag(Omega,tau);
        y_delta[t] ~ multi_normal(rep_vector(0,2),Sigma);
    }
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Challenging stochastic vol model
parts:
Is it slow in number of effective samples per iteraiton
or slow per iteration?

For efficiency per iteration, a Cholesky factor parameterization
of the correlation and covariance matrices coupled with
multi_normal_cholesky() should be more efficient.

Although it's not generalizable, given that you only
have a 2 x 2 corellation matrix, you could reparameterize
as two variances > 0 and a correlation in (-1,1) and put
a Beta prior on the correlation. If you want to leave it
as is, you'd be better off with a Cholesky factor
parameterization.

Put the rep_vector(0,2) in transformed data --- everything
that's constant should go in transformed data.

You can also calculate y_delta[,2] using vector head
and tail, then you'd break apart the loop from 1:T into
the 1 case and 2:T cases.

You could also move the definition of y_delta into the model
to avoid writing it out every iteration.

- Bob
